assertion.rationale: F1: data-api had ingressExternal:true and zero inbound authentication (app.ts:56) — anyone who found the FQDN could read Defender posture, Dependabot alerts and Log Analytics results, and loop full table scans. F1 is now CLOSED (Task 6): infra/bicep/apps/main.bicep's dataApiApp module sets ingressExternal:false, so the app is reachable only from inside the Container Apps environment. Both frontends already proxied /api/ server-side before this change — control-tower's and launch-ops' nginx.conf.template both carry a `location /api/ { proxy_pass ${DATA_API_ORIGIN}/; ... }` rule, verified present in both rather than assumed — so no legitimate caller lost access; DATA_API_ORIGIN still resolves the app's FQDN, which Azure Container Apps assigns to internal-ingress apps too. The /healthz convenience the app's header comment previously cited is now reached with `az containerapp exec` instead of a browser. F2: the MCP auth gate was inert in the shipped configuration — it threw only in backendMode 'cloud', MLS_TOOL_BACKENDS is set nowhere in infra/ or .github/, so /healthz reported auth.enforced:false to anyone. F2 is now CLOSED (Tasks 4 and 5). Task 4 closed the application half: loadInboundAuth (auth-gate.ts) no longer conditions enforcement on backendMode, so local mode — the configuration that actually ships — now fails closed at boot without MCP_AUTH_TOKEN or an explicit MCP_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED opt-out, and the gate is mounted ahead of the body parser. Task 5 closed the infra half: infra/bicep/apps/main.bicep no longer declares a `@secure()` mcpAuthToken parameter (deleted, along with demo.bicepparam's empty default); the mcp-tools container app instead resolves the mcp-auth-token secret directly from the platform Key Vault at runtime via a keyVaultUrl + identity reference, using a Key Vault Secrets User grant on the mcp-tools UAMI (module mcpKvGrant, reusing modules/key-vault-secrets-user-role.bicep, previously unreferenced since the 2026-08-24 Anthropic removal). The token therefore never enters this template, demo.bicepparam, ARM deployment history or a what-if log, and no workflow reads or exports it. MLS_TOOL_BACKENDS is now set explicitly via the mcpToolsBackendMode parameter (default 'local') instead of being absent from every workflow. F3: the Direct Line token endpoint minted tokens to unauthenticated callers whenever DIRECTLINE_ALLOWED_ORIGINS was unset or Origin was absent, and that path carries the MCP token, which made F2's gate irrelevant to it. F3 is now CLOSED (Task 7): directline-token.mjs now refuses with 500 when the allow-list is unset (so an unbound token is never minted) and with 403 when Origin is absent or not allow-listed, checked as two separate conditions rather than one combined boolean so neither can skip the other. F13: zero workload RBAC is expressed anywhere in IaC — the only role assignments in the estate are deployer-to-Owner and verifier-to-Reader, both at subscription scope in PowerShell; seven documented workload grants (data-api, mcp-tools, cost-ingest) exist nowhere as code, so access is not limited to authorized users, processes or devices by construction. Task 12 expresses five of the seven in code: infra/bicep/apps/main.bicep now grants data-api and mcp-tools Log Analytics Reader (scoped to the platform LAW, modules/log-analytics-reader-role.bicep) and Security Reader (subscription scope, modules/workload-role-assignments.bicep), mcp-tools additionally gets Cost Management Reader (same module), data-api's SQL contained-database user is expressed in data/seed/sql/900-contained-users.sql, and data-api's Fabric workspace Viewer grant is expressed via a new Add-FabricWorkspaceRoleAssignment function in infra/fabric/fabric-api.psm1, reached through provision-workspace.ps1's -DataApiPrincipalId parameter. CORRECTION (F24, final branch review): an earlier revision of this sentence said that parameter was 'wired'. It was not - nothing passed it, and layer-05-fabric.yml structurally could not, because L5 runs before L7 creates the identity. The capability existed; the invocation did not. F24 added the post-L7 step in layer-07-apps.yml that actually passes it, mirroring the F20 step Task 22 added for the SQL grant. So five of F13's seven grants landed in Task 12/17, the sixth landed with F24, and the seventh remains blocked on F19. Task 17 (F15, now CLOSED) lands the sixth: `az costmanagement export create`/`update` has no `--identity-type` flag, and the costmanagement CLI extension pins API version 2020-06-01, which hard-requires the destination storage account's shared keys to be enabled (github.com/Azure/azure-cli/issues/32912) — it 400s outright against this account's `allowSharedKeyAccess: false`. layer-06-platform.yml therefore creates the export via `az rest` against the Exports REST API directly (api-version 2023-08-01), requesting `identity: { type: SystemAssigned }` in the PUT body, and grants that identity's `principalId` (read back from the same PUT response, never a resourceId or clientId) Storage Blob Data Contributor via an explicit `az role assignment create`, scoped to the `cost-exports` container. One of the seven remains unexpressed and F13 stays OPEN because of it: cost-ingest -> Storage Blob Data Reader is blocked on F19 (cost-ingest has no Function App, and therefore no identity, anywhere in this repo's IaC, despite infra-up.yml:31 claiming otherwise). Building Task 12 also surfaced F20 (the SQL grant above is expressed but nothing re-ran the seed script after L7 creates the identity, so it did not yet apply in a single infra-up.yml pass — CLOSED by Task 22, which added a -SchemaOnly mode to data/seed/seed.ps1 / sql-seed.psm1's Invoke-SqlSeed, applying data/seed/sql/*.sql without requiring data/generated/ or a row-count check, invoked from layer-07-apps.yml's deploy job right after the apps deployment so the identity already exists) and F21 (mls-verifier's own documented Fabric workspace Viewer grant did not exist either, breaking the L5 Verifier audit — a different principal, tracked separately; CLOSED by Task 21, which wires provision-workspace.ps1's -VerifierPrincipalId — reusing the same Add-FabricWorkspaceRoleAssignment path this control's F13 grant above already uses — through layer-05-fabric.yml's deploy job, which resolves mls-verifier's service-principal object ID via `az ad sp show`). F20 and F21 were never contributors to this control (its evidence array above cites F1/F2/F3/F13 only; F20 maps to no 800-171 control per compliance/findings/2026-08-26-prepublication-review.md#f20, F21 likewise per .../#f21) — noted here only because this rationale referenced them in passing, and that reference must stay accurate. Overall status stays GAP: F1, F2 and F3 are all now closed, but F13 remains open — six of seven grants landed, one did not (F19) — and is this control's only remaining contributor.

recommendation: Close the one remaining grant: F19 must be fixed (cost-ingest provisioned as a real Function App with its own identity) before its Storage Blob Data Reader grant can be expressed at all. Add a criterion asserting each principal holds exactly its expected roles once it lands. (Setting ingressExternal:false on data-api, the MCP auth gate default and Key Vault token resolution, the Direct Line origin guard fail-closed fix, five of F13's seven workload RBAC grants, and the Cost Management service's Storage Blob Data Contributor grant recommended here previously, are all DONE — Tasks 4, 5, 6, 7, 12 and 17.)
